extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: Vibravox is a GDPR-compliant dataset containing audio recordings captured simultaneously using five body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) alongside an airborne reference microphone. It contains over 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants across clean and 3D spatialized noise conditions.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, Éric Bavu
extraction.citeAs: J. Hauret, M. Olivier, C. Langrenne, S. Poirée, and É. Bavu, 'vibravox (revision 071945b),' 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Audio signals were simultaneously recorded across six channels (one airborne reference microphone and five body-conduction audio sensors) using a Zoom F8n field recorder at 48 kHz and 32-bit resolution. Data collection comprised four consecutive steps per participant: speech-clean (reading French Wikipedia sentences for 15 minutes), speechless-noisy (remaining silent while free to move and breathe naturally in a 56-loudspeaker 3D ambisonics spatialization sphere replaying AudioSet noise for 2 minutes 24 seconds), speechless-clean (54 seconds of complete silence to capture physiological and sensor self-noise), and speech-noisy (reading for 54 seconds in 3D spatialized ambient noise from concert and street recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Experiments, Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A total of 30,568 sentences from 200 participants were initially gathered; 12 participants (6%) and 2,097 sentences (6.8%) were removed during post-processing due to mispronunciations, sensor displacement, sensor malfunctions, unequipped sensors, or failure to meet quality filtering criteria. Inadequate acoustic sealing also occurred when participants' ear canals were too small for the rigid in-ear sensor.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw 6-channel audio captured with a Zoom F8n field recorder at 48 kHz and 32-bit resolution. Text prompts were drawn from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Noise playback was sourced from AudioSet and in-house 3rd- and 5th-order ambisonic recordings of concerts and street events.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter was uniformly applied to each recording channel to attenuate low-frequency noise and mechanical artifacts. Voice Activity Detection (VAD) segment boundaries were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, with boundary trimming of 15 ms applied if extended segments exceeded audio limits.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization included lowercasing, punctuation removal (except apostrophes), and filtering out sentences containing numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, syntactic errors, or proper names (retaining only common first names, French towns/regions, and countries). Audio recordings were filtered using three criteria: Phoneme Error Rate (PER < 10% calculated via whisper-timestamped against labeled phonetic text), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR > 1.5 dB between voiced and unvoiced segments), and sensor sensitivity drift checking (Lspeech_50 > Lsilence_50).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Phonetic transcriptions into the 33-phoneme International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) for French were generated automatically from normalized text using the CoML lab text phonemizer. Manual phonetic transcription was performed for unrecognized words that triggered unwanted language switches (e.g., 'algorithme').
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Phoneme Error Rate (PER) was computed via Levenshtein distance between whisper-timestamped decoded speech and labeled phonetic transcriptions, discarding samples with PER > 10% to eliminate discrepancies caused by participant mispronunciation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Biometric voice data, physiological acoustic signals (heart rate, breathing), gender, and age.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables robust communication, speech enhancement, automatic speech recognition, and speaker verification in high-noise environments such as industrial and military operations; potential utility for vital signs tracking, life signals monitoring, and assistive technologies.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is exclusively in French. Participants are predominantly young adults (median age 25 years, overall mean age 28.55 years, range 18-82 years).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Body-conduction audio sensors suffer from intrinsic high-frequency loss due to physiological tissue attenuation. In-ear microphones are susceptible to varying acoustic sealing quality due to individual ear canal morphology. The temple vibration pickup exhibits a low signal-to-self-noise ratio. The speech-noisy subset lacks a clean reference signal.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and benchmarking of machine learning models for speech bandwidth extension (speech enhancement/super-resolution), speech-to-phonemes recognition (ASR), speaker verification, noise robustness analysis, and physiological noise analysis.
